text:
ash: Trying to script onboarding for CI: `redwoodctl login --non-interactive --profile=ci` inside our Windows installer. It just hangs (no browser). Anyone have a stable non-interactive/headless flow?

simon: We use `--device-code` in CI. It prints a URL + code, you can exchange it server-side. Does your installer expect no human input at all?

ash: Right — completely unattended. We spawn it from an installer service and want it to finish with creds in the profile keychain. `--device-code` still waits for the code to be entered.

maria: FWIW there's a small quirk on Windows: the Windows Credential Manager helper sometimes writes to the default profile instead of the one passed in `--profile` when the process runs as SYSTEM. We work around it by exporting `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE=ci` in the service environment before calling login.

ash: Ah that matches what I'm seeing — creds show up but under `default`. Can you share the exact env trick?

maria: We do something like:```bash
export REDWOODCTL_PROFILE=ci
export REDWOODCTL_NONINTERACTIVE=1   # our internal flag to avoid spawning browser
redwoodctl login --device-code
```
It still prints the device-code flow, but we have a small automation that polls the token endpoint using the code and finishes the exchange. Ugly but works.

jen: There is also a bug filed where the credential helper ignores the `--profile` arg if it can't access the interactive keyring (running as SYSTEM). I've bumped it in our tracker: https://go/repo/issue/4521 (internal).

ash: Thanks — will try the env workaround. For macOS localtest we don't have the SYSTEM problem but the CLI opens a browser even with `--non-interactive` sometimes. Any flags to force device-code/tty?

 taylor: `--device-code` should force device flow. If you see browser pop it probably falls back because `stdin`/`stdout` is a TTY. In automation wrap it like `redwoodctl login --device-code < /dev/null` or set `TERM=dumb` to make it noninteractive.

ash: Nice tip. I tried `TERM=dumb redwoodctl login --device-code < /dev/null --profile=ci` and it ran without opening a browser but creds still ended in `default` on Windows.

simon: For the Windows SYSTEM case you might need to specify the credential helper explicitly: `redwoodctl login --device-code --credential-helper=wincred --profile=ci` (assuming `wincred` is what we ship on that host). That forces the correct helper rather than the auto-detect.

ash: Tested that too — explicit helper + `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE=ci` made it behave. Thanks all.

devx-bot: Docs: redwoodctl auth automation guide -> https://docs.redwood.com/cli/auth-automation (internal). Also: open a small repro and tag @devex for a follow-up so we can add a CI mode flag. :sparkles:

ash: Filing a tiny notes PR against docs and the issue: https://go/repo/pull/789 (adds advice for `REDWOODCTL_PROFILE`, `--device-code`, and `--credential-helper`). Leaving this thread in case someone else hits it.

maria: ++ please add a short note about the SYSTEM/credential-manager behavior; saved us time.

jen: We should add an integration test for noninteractive install scenarios (Windows service + SYSTEM). I'll add it to the queue.

ash: Closing for now — patch + docs landed in our internal fork. If it resurfaces I'll reopen. :white_check_mark:
